headline: Two crude bombs thrown outside Prime Minister’s Office in Dhaka
summary: One bomb exploded while the other was defused by the bomb disposal unit. Police are now reviewing CCTV footage to identify the suspects.
details: Two people on a motorcycle threw two crude bombs outside the Prime Minister's Office in Dhaka's Tejgaon area late Friday night.
The incident occurred around 1:30 am on Saturday, according to Ibne Mizan, deputy commissioner of police for the Tejgaon Division.
One of the bombs exploded upon impact, while the second remained unexploded. The Dhaka Metropolitan Police's bomb disposal unit rushed to the scene and safely defused the device.
Police report that the suspects arrived on a motorcycle, waited for a few minutes, and looked around before throwing the bombs and fleeing towards Mirpur Road via Agargaon.
Authorities have begun work to identify those involved and are currently collecting CCTV footage from nearby cameras to track the suspects.
caption:
Two crude bombs were hurled at the Prime Minister's Office in Dhaka late at night. One exploded, while the other was defused by police.

Two people on a motorcycle threw two crude bombs outside the Prime Minister's Office in Dhaka's Tejgaon area late Friday night.

The incident occurred around 1:30 am on Saturday, according to Ibne Mizan, deputy commissioner of police for the Tejgaon Division.

One of the bombs exploded upon impact, while the second remained unexploded. The Dhaka Metropolitan Police's bomb disposal unit rushed to the scene and safely defused the device.

Police report that the suspects arrived on a motorcycle, waited for a few minutes, and looked around before throwing the bombs and fleeing towards Mirpur Road via Agargaon.

Authorities have begun work to identify those involved and are currently collecting CCTV footage from nearby cameras to track the suspects.

headline: BGB returns fire after BSF shooting leaves Bangladeshi injured
summary: The Border Guard Bangladesh responded in self-defence after BSF members allegedly shot a Bangladeshi national inside Indian territory in Kushtia.
details: The Border Guard Bangladesh (BGB) returned fire this morning after members of the Border Security Force (BSF) allegedly shot and injured a Bangladeshi national.
The incident occurred around 9:30 am, approximately 300 yards inside Indian territory, opposite the Jamalpur border in Kushtia’s Daulatpur upazila.
Lt Col Rashed Kamal Roni, commanding officer of 47 BGB Kushtia Battalion, confirmed that the injured person is a Bangladeshi citizen based on preliminary information.
A BGB patrol team responded promptly and returned fire in self-defence to ensure the safety of people on the Bangladesh side.
Patrols and surveillance along the border have been intensified to maintain stability and ensure the country's sovereignty.
The BGB stated they remain vigilant and professional in responding to potential incidents and are raising awareness to discourage unauthorised activities in border areas.
